failed_edge: The argument passes from the n=4 condition for the single fixed value Y=y^2 to a divisibility assertion for every positive-square value of Y.
quote: The condition is that \(16Y+1 \mid P(Y)\) for all \(Y \in \{1^2, 2^2, 3^2, \dots\}\) (i.e., for all \(Y=y^2\) where \(y \in \mathbb{Z}^+\)).
reason: In the theorem, y is one fixed positive integer; only n is universally quantified. Thus n=4 yields \(16y^2+1\mid P(y^2)\) at one value, not for arbitrarily large y. Consequently the step forcing the constant remainder \(R_0\) to vanish is unsupported, so the claimed contradiction does not follow.
